title: claimspec v1 — claims file
description: What must be true, and how to try to falsify it. A claim is a statement the project makes; each fault is one concrete way that statement could be false, expressed as a deterministic source change. This file is code: its `replace` strings execute under the test runner. Treat it with the same review discipline as source.

id.description: Stable identifier. Renaming it changes every fingerprint derived from it.

statement.description: The claim in plain language, as the project states it.

source.description: Where the claim comes from. Spec- and ADR-sourced claims are human-governed; annotation- and comment-sourced claims may have been written by the same agent that wrote the tests, and should be ranked accordingly.

defendedBy.description: Globs (project-relative) for the test files that supposedly defend this claim. Empty or absent means: discover defenders as the test files that import each fault's target file (relative paths and resolved aliases). If nothing resolves, the verdict is `nocover`.

fault.description: One concrete way the claim could be false, and how a tool would try to make it so. `method` says which; it defaults to `fault-injection`, whose shape is an exact-string substitution and is unchanged. Producer-agnostic: a human, an operator, an agent or a derivation may all emit this shape, and every artifact says which.

find.description: Exact text to locate in `file`. Must occur exactly `expectHits` times or the fault is `unverifiable`.

replace.description: Exact replacement text. May be empty.

expectHits.description: How many times `find` must occur in `file`. Any other count means the anchor has rotted or is ambiguous → `unverifiable`, never a silent skip.

methodDetail.description: Data belonging to a method the spec has not specified yet. `assertion` and `scan` are reserved names with no required fields, so a tool adopting one needs somewhere to put the rule it checked and the place it checked — without which it can declare that a probe exists and nothing about it. Deliberately unconstrained, deliberately namespaced, and **forbidden under `fault-injection`**, whose shape IS specified and must not acquire a junk drawer. What the first real consumer puts here is the evidence for what the specified shape should become; it is a staging area, not a permanent home.

then.$comment: The default method. Absent `method` means fault-injection, so every claims file written before the field existed is held to exactly the same requirements as before. The property stubs are what ajv's strict mode needs to accept `required` here; the real definitions stay above.
